label: Sequence start: first token from {s,u,v,x,b,3,i,j,e}, or early copy steps of short sequences
explanation: Two position-locked components, both near the start of a phase. (1) At t=0, gated by token identity: active on about 30% of first steps, concentrated on s,u,v,x,b,3,i,j,e (rate 10-20%+ per token at t=0 vs ~3% for others such as f,1,h). This gives about 29% of mass but low per-step magnitude (~0.08-0.12 of max). (2) Copy-phase steps t=4-5, i.e. the first one or two outputs after <DEL> when L=3 or 4 (recall_idx 1-2). This is about 50% of mass and holds all the strongest activations; top examples are recall_idx=1 in L=3 sequences (input = orig(0), activation ~0.9-1.0 of max), and token identity matters less here. Activation and firing rate fall off sharply with L (L=3 rate 35%, L=4 17%, L>=5 under 5%). Weaker leftovers the predicate misses: t=1 (about 9% of mass, many false positives) and scattered copy steps at recall_idx 1-5 in longer sequences. Silent at the delimiter step, at original positions t>=3, and at late copy steps. Dev P=0.88, R=0.69, F1=0.77, mass recall 0.80.
